beur-hagra/1:א: (א) And he takes the matzot, etc., and grasps them. Magen Avraham. And as above siman 473 and as Gemara says he holds two, etc.
beur-hagra/1:ב: (ב) And he blesses, etc., and afterward. Per Rishonim in Tosafot Berachot 39b s.v. hakol that one blesses HaMotzi on the whole and on eating matzah on the broken lechem oni; but all on the broken — not because one does not make mitzvot bundled as bundles, as chapter Afikoman 102b and R' Menachem blessed all on the broken saying it is not called bundles here like kiddush cup where one blesses wine blessing and kiddush; and if one has only lettuce one blesses borei peri haadamah and on eating maror at first dipping; R' Yitzchak removed himself from dispute and did as written here — Rosh wrote.
beur-hagra/1:ג: (ג) And then he will do. As such, it is written and destroyed
beur-hagra/1:ה: (ה) And baptized in salt. Jerusalem and Tayya are in salt:
beur-hagra/1:ו: (ו) And the custom is not. As in Berachot 40a: there is none, etc.
beur-hagra/1:ז: (ז) And eat for the reason. According to C:
beur-hagra/1:ח: (ח) together as a. If the owner's body is sick. It has been given to him, and he has to do so with him:
beur-hagra/1:ט: (ט) If not. It is necessary to eat all the rods together as “the name of the Kield B.”
beur-hagra/1:כ: (כ) Third matza. As explained Pesachim 117b: each one, etc.; and as Yerushalmi chapter 3 of Shekalim halacha 4 regarding terumat haGes — take from first even if first has, return to second, etc.
beur-hagra/1:ל: (ל) Selecting. Because of the glory, and the glory was made:
beur-hagra/1:מ: (מ) And some say. There is no concern of kapa as Yerushalmi: all that has bread substance has no kapa concern; see Maggid Mishneh.
beur-hagra/1:נ: (נ) The reason. Because of a thirst. Demeror does not impede the cause as a result of the release of the cause, and it is also the reason that he does:
beur-hagra/1:ס: (ס) And from when he blesses, etc., in order. Taz: for Hillel he only fulfills with this and it is interruption.
beur-hagra/4:א: (א) (ד) If he ate, etc. — e.g. they forced him; although we hold mitzvot require intention, we do not hold like Rava there 'this teaches' but as stated there; see Rashi, Ran.
beur-hagra/4:ב: (ב) (ד) But if. Madalla was taken swaying. Name.
beur-hagra/7:א: (א) (ז) And they practice. As chapter HaTodah: three mitzvot come from an issaron.
beur-hagra/7:ב: (ב) Commemoration, etc. One exiting prison must give thanks as chapter 9 of Berachot; we say in thanksgiving offering if he baked four loaves — one for chametz and three for matzot.
beur-hagra/7:ג: (ג) They do them as a. It was written in the verses, and it was written in them:
beur-hagra/7:ד: (ד) (ז) If one changed. As Megillah 21b: second called, third called, etc.
chok-yaakov/1:א: (א) He should wash his hands. The Gemara's wording: even though he already washed once, since he must recite the Haggadah we are concerned lest he diverted his attention and touched an unclean place. Beit Yosef wrote one should not intend at the first washing to complete the entire meal without diverting attention, so as not to nullify the Sages' enactment of washing twice on this night, end of his words. His intent: since the Gemara says one must wash a second time lest he diverted attention — we cannot outsmart the Sages' decree and say he will not divert and wash only once. His words are correct and such is the custom; Bach and Taz criticized him in vain.
chok-yaakov/1:ב: (ב) And he grasps them in his hand — because there are divided opinions on which to bless HaMotzi and which for eating matza, or to bless both on one; therefore he grasps all in his hand to fulfill all opinions. Maharil wrote: he grasps three matzot in his hand — the upper for HaMotzi, the third for lechem mishneh, and the broken for lechem oni; he blesses HaMotzi, sets aside the third, blesses on the broken with the upper still grasped for eating matza, and blesses both blessings before breaking them, end of his words; and Acharonim agreed.
chok-yaakov/1:ג: (ג) And on eating matza — that which we bless HaMotzi and not on eating matza; see siman 473.
chok-yaakov/1:ד: (ד) And the custom is not to dip in salt on the first night — Maharil wrote because of affection for matza; Levush wrote the reason is lechem oni. The rest of the year the custom is to dip even plain bread; and so all Pesach days except the first two nights; and the first night the Rav wrote is not precise, and Maharil wrote explicitly, see there.
chok-yaakov/1:ה: (ה) And he eats them while leaning together — the reason appears simple, also for the view that one blesses on the whole HaMotzi and on the broken for eating matza or vice versa: one cannot bless and eat them sequentially, for if he blesses HaMotzi first and eats, how can he afterward bless on eating matza since he already ate matza; and likewise he cannot bless first on eating matza and eat, for plainly he cannot since he did not bless HaMotzi; therefore he must bless both blessings first. If he then eats the broken of HaMotzi alone there is interruption between the blessing on matza and its eating, and likewise the reverse; therefore he eats together so there is no interruption. Nevertheless if he cannot eat together he eats sequentially and it is not interruption after the fact since it is eating-related; see siman 167. The reason of the Rishonim is simple; see Acharonim who wrote other reasons — per my words this is the essential reason. Bach and Taz challenged in the name of Maharal of Prague how he eats together, for we say in chapter HaIsh Mekadesh (and Eruvin 50) that what is not one after the other even in one gulp does not apply — see their answers; in my opinion there is no question here at all, for many mitzvot require specifically one gulp, such as Hillel's view of matza and maror, and the four species of lulav; specifically there regarding kiddushin of two sisters — if he betrothed one she is betrothed and the second betrothed afterward is not; therefore even in one gulp she is not betrothed; not so here where the mitzvah is specifically both together, not one alone nor sequentially, for such is their mitzvah together — and it is simple.
chok-yaakov/1:ו: (ו) A kezayit from each — it implies the broken of HaMotzi also needs a kezayit; so too Magen Avraham; see Taz what he wrote.
chok-yaakov/1:ז: (ז) He eats HaMotzi first — see above siman 472 seif 16 where I wrote in the name of Maharai that the kezayit of HaMotzi does not require leaning; but from Tur's words both require leaning, and so is practiced. Magen Avraham wrote in any case l'chatchila one should swallow a crushed kezayit in one gulp, and after the fact even little by little if he does not delay between them longer than eating a peras; and likewise maror — even l'chatchila if difficult to swallow together, end of his words.
chok-yaakov/1:ח: (ח) And he submerges it entirely in charoset — to kill poison in it; he does not bless until after dipping before eating, for it is preparatory to the act; as explained above siman 473 seif 6 regarding first dipping, not like Maharil; so too Magen Avraham there.
chok-yaakov/1:ט: (ט) Without leaning — since it is commemoration of servitude; if he wishes to lean he may.
chok-yaakov/1:י: (י) And he wraps it with maror — so Pesachim 116a: Hillel and the Rabbis dispute when the Temple stood whether one wrapped matzah and maror together or each alone; and the Gemara states: now that the halacha was not stated neither like one nor like the other, we practice both — first eat each separately, then both together; and so Rambam, Rosh, and Tur; and I saw in Beit Hillel siman 298 seif dalet wondering on Rosh, Tur, and Beit Yosef for ruling plainly there that prohibitions nullify each other; he wrote: wondrous wonder that it was hidden from them what is stated in chapter of mixtures 99a on the view of R' Eliezer who said: just as mitzvot do not nullify each other, so prohibitions do not nullify each other — who heard that one who said mitzvot do not nullify each other? Hillel, as taught: they said of Hillel the Elder he wrapped them in one bite and ate, because of 'on matzot and marorim you shall eat it'; and since in this Gemara the law of prohibitions not nullifying depends on it, logically mitzvot do not nullify each other like Hillel who wrapped together; and we rule in chapter Afikoman to fulfill all — taste and see; why rule here leniently that prohibitions do not nullify? End Beit Hillel's wonder, and he strains greatly to answer — see there; and in my opinion there is not even a slight question, for his words that these two laws depend on each other — why does the Gemara say 'and it disputes R' Eliezer' and not 'they dispute Hillel'? It is certain and simple the Gemara means: and they dispute R' Eliezer who said just as mitzvot do not nullify each other, so prohibitions do not nullify each other; and Resh Lakish holds we do not say this 'just as' — rather although mitzvot do not nullify each other, since both are for one intent — remembrance of the Exodus — nevertheless prohibitions nullify each other; and this is simple and clear; this requires further study; and what he further challenges that they ruled against Rambam — I sensed this in my book Maaseh Yehoshua general rule 80 seif mem alef — see there.
chok-yaakov/1:כ: (כ) And so I have seen practiced — Acharonim agreed to dip in charoset; Magen Avraham wrote where customary it is customary.
chok-yaakov/1:ל: (ל) And he says remembrance for the Temple — Aruch entry zayin kuf resh: remembrance for the Temple like Hillel — when the Temple stood Hillel wrapped matzah and maror and ate in one bite, since both are from the Torah one does not nullify the other; but now matzah is d'oraisa as written 'in the evening you shall eat matzot' and maror is d'rabbanan — forbidden to eat them in one bite, for d'rabbanan comes and nullifies d'oraisa; therefore eat first each alone, then both together in one bite — remembrance for the Temple like Hillel; and since eating is only for remembrance, one does not bless on it — end; and accordingly one can also reconcile Rambam chapter 8 laws of chametz, and escape Ra'avad's challenge who ruled when the Temple stood one eats matzah and maror together or sequentially because there is no stringency if eating together since they do not nullify each other; and especially per your view that prohibitions do not nullify each other — although halacha was not stated, nevertheless practice like the master and one may eat them l'chatchila in one bite specifically, as the baraita's language implies, better than now when maror d'rabbanan nullifies matzah d'oraisa — therefore we practice both; and in responsa Shaarei Ephraim simanim 153-154 they expanded to reconcile Rambam — and per my words it is clear and correct.
chok-yaakov/1:מ: (מ) Like Hillel — our formula is so; so Hillel did when the Temple stood — he wrapped matzah and maror and ate, etc.; Taz wrote one may say he wrapped Pesach, matzah, and maror as Rashi explained in the three — so Hillel did — end; and in truth Rashi explained so, and so Rosh, Tur, and Tosafot Pesachim 120a s.v. be'achrona; but Rambam chapter 1 laws of chametz wrote even when the Temple stood they did not wrap the Pesach with matzah and maror, only afterward the Pesach; and it is reasonable like him per the verse in parashat Beha'alotcha 'on matzot and marorim you shall eat it' — meaning on the matzah and maror you shall eat the Pesach; and so the sugya implies — only on matzah and maror it says they ate together; and even per poskim who also wrapped Pesach with them when the Temple stood, nevertheless our formula is correct: since we say 'so he did' and now there is no Pesach, one should not mention Pesach, lest he speak falsely since he has no Pesach; and also it misleads, for mentioning Pesach and saying 'so he did' may lead to eating roasted meat with it and appear like eating kodashim outside — therefore do not change the old formula; and in the Sephardic formula in Pesach Ma'uvin he does not mention anything, only Hillel who wrapped and ate in one bite.
chok-yaakov/1:נ: (נ) He should not speak — Shelah wrote he should not speak at all until after eating afikoman; and the blessing on matza must also intend afikoman; this is extra stringency against poskim' implication, and truly impossible to guard throughout the meal; certainly the blessing applies to the whole meal, and what if he pauses — all year we interrupt during a meal though the first blessing applies until meal's end. That he not speak before the korekh is because some hold the essential mitzvah is specifically the korekh and one must bless on it; therefore no speech until korekh to fulfill all views; see Beit Yosef.
chok-yaakov/1:ס: (ס) Until he eats the wrap — and if he transgressed and spoke, the agreement of Acharonim is he need not return and bless, only l'chatchila he should be careful.
chok-yaakov/2:_: At first dipping with Borei peri ha'adamah — Magen Avraham wrote: only if he takes that type of maror fit to eat raw does one bless on it; but what is not normally eaten raw, like tamcha called horseradish — one blesses only on eating maror, as pepper explained in siman 202 where one does not bless on it, end of his words. In truth Gemara and all poskim imply clearly that for all types of maror one blesses Borei peri ha'adamah even if not eaten raw; the reason must be since through dipping in vinegar etc. it becomes edible; and further one can say these enjoyment-blessings are like blessing on the mitzvah, as explained below siman 484; therefore we bless at dipping with Borei peri ha'adamah and on eating maror — simple and clear; see siman 210.
chok-yaakov/3:_: If he swallowed matza he fulfilled — but l'chatchila he should chew until crushed and then swallow, as maror; see Acharonim who distinguish cooked matza in siman 461.
chok-yaakov/4:א: (א) Without intention — Magen Avraham wrote: even though mitzvot require intention as siman 60 seif 4, for eating it is different since he ate and enjoyed, end of his words; so too Tosafot chapter Arvei Pesachim (Pesachim 115); see Beit Yosef in the name of Ran and Maggid Mishneh. Requires slight study, for sugya in Rosh Hashana 28 implies perhaps no distinction; see Lechem Mishneh laws of shofar; Gemara and poskim explain the same for maror if eaten without intention; see Bach who wrote even per poskim matza requires intention, maror d'rabbanan all agree does not require intention — this too in Tosafot Rosh Hashana 28 s.v. amar Rava; and Magen Avraham siman 60 seif 3 in the name of Acharonim' responsa. Therefore possible for maror even if he did not know it was maror or thought it was a weekday he fulfilled — so appears to me essentially.
chok-yaakov/4:ב: (ב) He did not fulfill — poskim' meaning: on the second night he did not fulfill, for even the second day d'rabbanan we do not treat lightly; see siman 496. Magen Avraham challenged in siman 204 seif 8 where Rama wrote if forced to eat or drink, even if he enjoyed he does not bless on it — yet here Mechaber ruled if forced to eat matza he fulfilled; see there.
chok-yaakov/5:א: (א) Because that eating — even without this reason he should be obligated, for during his insanity he did not know it was Pesach and he was obligated to eat matza as above seif 4; this is not the intent, for nevertheless he also did not think it was a weekday or that this was not matza, and one would say he fulfilled; therefore this reason was needed; requires study; see Lechem Mishneh laws of shofar.
chok-yaakov/5:ב: (ב) He was exempt — nevertheless we do not say since pushed off it is pushed off, since the time of obligation still applies; see Taz here and Yoreh De'ah siman 396.
chok-yaakov/6:_: Between one eating and its fellow more than eating a peras — such is the Gemara's wording in chapter Afikoman; truly explained below siman 612 in Gemara, Tosafot, and all poskim, see there in Beit Yosef: from start of first eating until end of last eating if more than eating a peras they do not combine; therefore 'between one eating and its fellow' here is not precise; so Magen Avraham; and it is clear not like Rosh Yosef who makes distinctions. Tur and Rokeach siman 488 appear they preserved this and wrote 'between eating and eating' like peras — their intent, it appears to me, is with the eating it is more than peras; and this is why they said if from start of eating to end is more than peras, there is between first chewing and last chewing interruption of peras, therefore they do not combine for the measure. We find Tur precisely wrote here like peras, and below siman 612 explains more than peras does not combine is also from one time, start to end of eating; here it says between eating and eating — both are one time, not like R' Yosef who wrote on Tur here that his words are imprecise; Mechaber did not want to change Gemara wording and relied on siman 612; see measure of eating peras how much; Taz wrote even if he did not pause the measure he fulfilled, nevertheless it is mitzvah min hamuvchar to swallow kezayit matza and maror crushed in one time.
chok-yaakov/7:א: (א) No obligation to eat matza — Magen Avraham in the name of Ran: although obligated to eat bread on Yom Tov, nevertheless he may use rich matza, end of his words; Terumat HaDeshen siman 58 wrote in Semag, and one proves from here he is not obligated to eat bread on Yom Tov; so I found in Tosafot Sukkah 20a s.v. iy ba'i he is not obligated to eat bread except the first Yom Tov night of Pesach and Sukkot; see Magen Avraham siman 188 seif 9.
chok-yaakov/7:ב: (ב) Only the first night — Kol Bo siman 50; and the reason we do not bless on eating matza only the first nights: from then on it is optional; and eating matza is only because one cannot eat chametz — like one who eats kosher animal meat and not non-kosher, for which one does not bless since that eating is only bodily need to satisfy hunger, not mitzvah. But eating in sukkah, though also optional other days, since sitting is not bodily need but mitzvah fulfillment, one should bless to sit in sukkah; see siman 639 in other words. Tosafot Sukkah 27a s.v. chazar bo: if he did not eat matza on Pesach night he has no compensation on other Pesach days — one can learn: one who did not eat matza on Pesach night due to coercion, when he eats matza later he does not bless on eating matza since it is optional with no compensation; requires study.
chok-yaakov/7:ג: (ג) Commemoration of thanksgiving loaves — Maharil wrote; and further called lechem oni, and a poor person brings a tenth of an ephah.
chok-yaakov/7:ד: (ד) And they make a sign on them — the Rav wrote in responsa siman 119 one should not make letters on matzah, for when breaking it is erasing on Yom Tov; see siman 340; Magen Avraham in the name of Mahariv: if he has many children and lacks challah measure, he may knead two doughs less than measure and combine them and make three matzot from both; Mahariv further wrote the second matzah should be larger than the others, since each must eat from it two pieces — one at motzi and one for afikoman — end; Maharil wrote: good to limit that matzot not exceed an isaron; but if there are four or five eggs more, no need to be particular — end; unlike Magen Avraham in the name of Darkhei Moshe in the name of Maharil to the contrary; see simanim 456-457 how we practice.
chok-yaakov/7:ה: (ה) If one of them broke — in these countries they make four matzot from the dough and call the fourth 'doubt matza' so if mishap occurs to one they take it, even though one should make only three like thanksgiving loaves; see Levush; perhaps they rely on the world since they make dough somewhat more than issaron — therefore make one extra matza from the surplus and only three from the issaron; and since it is for doubt there is no stringency.
chok-yaakov/7:ו: (ו) They take it for the second — even if the third broke; if so we prioritize the third before the second, nevertheless for mitzvah precedence one should not bake another, end Agur. In these countries they take the doubt matza so they do not prioritize and delay the second from its mitzvah; specifically if the third broke, not the first two — if one of the first two broke, it appears simple per Agur since there is no full delay of its mitzvah; on the contrary we elevate the second; if the first broke they take it for second so it not fully delayed from mitzvah; requires study; though hidur mitzvah that the second too is whole — as Maharshal wrote in responsa siman 88 — nevertheless such we do not delay it if broken after the fact.
peri-megadim/1:_: And he holds them in his hand — Taz. What he wrote 'he should hold both in his hand' — so Tur; and one may say Rosh Pesachim 116a wrote he breaks from the whole and broken as one and did not mention holding two, for per his view requiring lechem mishneh it is fitting to hold all three at motzi, then set aside the third and bless (motzi and) eating matzah on the whole and broken, intending to fulfill eating matzah through one of them as we will say below letter bet (see Maharil; and discarding the third from his hand is correct not to treat it lightly); if so, why did Tur write 'hold both'? And from what Taz wrote afterward it appears after it is not precise — rather hold all three together or bring them with the plate near him; correct to hold all three in hand as stated; and what Taz wrote in the name of Rashal — he challenged him: why bring from siman 476? Tur wrote here to break from both together for one who wishes to fulfill both; Rashal's intent is halacha is certainly like Rosh that on the whole motzi requiring lechem mishneh one holds all three, says motzi, breaks a bit to show the halacha, and remains somewhat connected — see siman 167 in Magen Avraham hei and Ateret Zekenim in the name of Bach and Rashal in Shabbat — one marks with a knife before the blessing — see there; possibly so here too; since still connected it is considered whole; nevertheless correct custom as Chayei Adam in the name of Maharil: hold all three, bless motzi, discard the lower from hand, intend eating matzah fulfilled through upper or broken, eat a kezayit from each since doubtful, intend on both — as stated; unlike one who holds motzi is primarily a kezayit on the whole — need not eat kezayit from motzi; see Darkei Moshe 476 explaining 'he should not break' meaning not separate entirely; and when eating two kezayit together or one after another if unable together, still need haseiba on both since doubtful — explained further letter bet and see 476.
peri-megadim/2:א: (א) And he eats — Taz. Behold in Berakhot 39b: on Pesach one places the broken inside the whole and breaks; there are three explanations: (1) Rosh Pesachim 116 — motzi on the whole requiring lechem mishneh with the third, and eating matzah on the broken as an impoverished person's way; therefore three matzot needed. (2) Gemara Yerushalmi in Semag — motzi on the broken as impoverished; do not make bundles of bundles; not fitting to bless two blessings on the broken — bless eating matzah on the whole; and Beit Yosef wrote Tosafot wrote thus — see Tosafot Berakhot 39b s.v. hakol. (3) Appears Rif's view in Beit Yosef — on the broken bless both motzi and eating matzah; so Ran; see Tosafot Pesachim on 'what' — therefore Rif on Pesach breaks on one and broken presumably places broken on whole as Berakhot states on Pesach — placed inside whole, meaning on the whole, within it, so it appears he breaks on the whole; nevertheless two blessings refer to the broken per Rif and Yerushalmi; only two matzot needed — one whole and one broken; for us three matzot — two wholes for lechem mishneh and broken in middle; doubtful whether motzi or eating matzah on it; at motzi hold all three, then discard lower third, bless eating matzah on both broken and upper — doubtful; Mechaber ruled eat a kezayit from each — doubtful whether eating matzah on whole or broken; l'chatchila put both in mouth — two kezayit together; not only for Rosh that whole is motzi and broken eating matzah — motzi eats first since he blessed on it earlier and after filling his appetite eats kezayit matzah as Bach wrote; and even per Mechaber who is doubtful, eat both together, for impossible to know which he eats with eating matzah blessing — must eat two kezayit within time of eating a meal portion; if cannot eat quickly, still two kezayit within meal portion time; nevertheless eat from motzi first, for there too he fulfills eating matzah — Bach and Perishah; but from Levush it implies both are eaten together because both are one mitzvah — motzi is not without matzah and matzah not without motzi — see there.
peri-megadim/2:ב: (ב) Maharal of Prague challenged: all not in one gulp even in one gulp does not apply — see Tur he eats together; if eats HaMotzi first without intending eating matzah likewise not in one gulp; see Beit Yosef; already explained; appears since Taz aimed at Levush as written.
peri-megadim/3:_: He will not be able to eat from what he has commanded, but he has done so, and he does not give up on the inventions, but if it has occurred to him that he has given some of the pieces that he has received, and he has a piece of fruit that he will not eat a piece of sway that does not pass away, and even if he does not have so much trouble
peri-megadim/4:_: Shake off — Taz twice, R' Chaim Pesachim 116b s.v. kapa: despite majority no worm in maror per Tosafot there, in danger we concern for minority; Rashi explained kapa poison in maror — see there; Levush brought both; Magen Avraham 473 note 19 whether blessing before dipping or after; Chok Yaakov here note 8.
peri-megadim/5:א: (א) Third matza to fulfill mitzvah in wrapping — Taz. So Rosh Pesachim 116a. We wrote for Rif two matzot suffice whole and broken; we make three as seif 7 Hagahah; even for Rosh HaMotzi on whole — then two suffice whole until HaMotzi, bless HaMotzi on lechem mishneh, then break second and bless eating matzah; perhaps must break before saying 'this poor bread' siman 473 seif 6; Levush there says Haggadah on lechem oni and children ask why hide half for afikoman.
peri-megadim/5:ב: (ב) It appears if on first night he has only two whole matzot he leaves them whole until HaMotzi, for lechem mishneh required — so Rosh Pesachim 116a distinguishes Pesach from other Yom Tov; breaking before 'this poor bread' is custom as Levush from Beit Yosef 473 Kol Bo — not in Talmud; Rambam chapter 8 law 6 breaks when saying HaMotzi; though we do not practice so, when impossible lechem mishneh certainly preferable as we say; see siman 482 one who is ill.
peri-megadim/6:_: And he submerges — Taz; see Levush wrote kapa language in wrapping since eating matza weakens person and does not harm; nevertheless since mentioned zecher lemikdash keHillel and he dipped in wrapping. I have not seen custom to dip in wrapping — see Eliyah Rabba note afterward.
peri-megadim/7:א: (א) In order — Taz. Pesachim 116a dispute: for Hillel in Temple times mitzvah l'chatchila to eat Pesach, matzah, and maror together (per Rashi and Rashbam there; but per Rambam chapter 8 law 6 from matzah only wraps matzah and maror in Yerushalmi) and b'dieved fulfills each separately; for Rabbis l'chatchila require each separately and b'dieved together — so Tosafot s.v. ella and Eliyah Rabbah letter zayin — see there; concludes there in our time eat first matzah alone and maror alone, then together — remembrance for the Temple like Hillel; Bach wrote now there is no mitzvah at all even d'rabbanan even for Hillel to eat matzah and maror together since there is no Pesach — see there; and this is Rashi and Rashbam who wrapped all three together for Hillel, unlike now without Pesach therefore say remembrance for the Temple; and obvious if he spoke between blessing and wrapping he need not return and bless; Tosafot s.v. ella bet wrote therefore now need each alone then both together — if eating both at once, maror d'rabbanan now nullifies matzah d'oraisa; if eating matzah first alone then matzah of rabbinic origin nullifies maror d'rabbanan now; and they wrote nevertheless if halacha were clear like Hillel, etc. — they meant Rabbis and d'rabbanan — one may explain they wrote it appears halacha like Hillel in Temple times wrapping matzah and maror (without Pesach), and so now wrapping is d'rabbanan; impossible now even for Hillel since maror d'rabbanan nullifies matzah d'oraisa — therefore even Hillel needs now l'chatchila each alone then both together d'rabbanan like Torah law; and on this they wrote nevertheless if halacha were clear like Hillel there would be another enactment — eat matzah first then matzah and maror in wrap, and matzah would not be optional d'rabbanan requiring wrap per Rambam who wraps matzah and maror without Pesach — therefore for us wrap is d'rabbanan like Torah law; but uncertain like whom is halacha — perhaps Rabbis, and matzah of rabbinic origin nullifies maror d'rabbanan — therefore need first each alone then both together lest Hillel; and if challenged 'remembrance for the Temple' — it is d'rabbanan mitzvah; impossible to say only d'rabbanan remembrance — rather one may say they say remembrance for the Temple in the wrap to inform that now one may not go out with wrap alone, which nullifies maror d'rabbanan to matzah d'oraisa; and because remembrance for the Temple there they would fulfill everything in wrap alone, both d'oraisa — as stated; nevertheless even now matzah d'rabbanan requires wrap for Hillel; and specifically l'chatchila each alone then wrap;
